subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: Should OpenClaw add a native OpenAI/Codex recovery-state contract plus brokered reauth execution, and what trust boundary should authorize the broker?
rationale: Current main has explicit private `/login codex` pairing, but automatically or brokeredly invoking host-side OAuth recovery would define a new security-sensitive auth and execution boundary that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
options.body: Define `quota_wait` and `reauth_required`-style state across provider, Gateway, and UI first, then add brokered execution behind explicit owner/operator authorization and audit requirements.

options.title: Keep explicit login only
options.body: Treat `/login codex` and terminal reauth as the supported recovery path for now, and close or narrow the brokered execution portion separately.

options.title: Move broker to plugin seam
options.body: Require the host-side reauth adapter to live behind a plugin or ClawHub-hosted integration API rather than core-specific command execution.

recommendation.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
recommendation.body: Define `quota_wait` and `reauth_required`-style state across provider, Gateway, and UI first, then add brokered execution behind explicit owner/operator authorization and audit requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider quota display, Gateway auth status, Control UI recovery, and security policy, and current history gives steipete the broadest routing signal.
